## 15. Repository and pins design

**Layout.** The repository is `ChristopherLinnett/craftbridge` (MIT OR Apache-2.0; private until hosted CI starts, then public, PD3), checked out at `artcraft-plugin-port/` (PD16). It has one folder per platform, each a complete build, and nothing of a platform at its root (PD19). A toolchain's build files sit only in its own platform folder: no `Cargo.toml`, `Package.swift` or Gradle build or settings file stands anywhere else — a cross-platform folder, another platform's folder or the plan, bar the probes kept under `plan/evidence/` — where no build would read it (AGENTS §1). Inside each platform folder the universal core sits beside the app plugin (PD10), and samples sit beside the library they consume (D-1).

**Dependency direction.** Within the core and within a plugin, dependencies point down the layers. `rust/xtask/src/layers.rs` lists each crate's layer once, and the gate fails on any edge the table does not allow (D-25).

| Layer | Crate | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| core 0 | `craftbridge-media` | external crates; `filmcraft-codecs` and `filmcraft-isobmff` at EffectCraft's FilmCraft revision (PD18) |
| core 1 | `craftbridge-core` | a lower core rank |
| core 2 | `craftbridge-core-ffi` | the lower core ranks; `uniffi` |
| app 0 | `craftbridge-effects` | any core crate; `effectcraft-*` |
| app 1 | `craftbridge-effects-ffi` | a lower rank of its app, and any core crate; `uniffi` |
| tool | `craftbridge-effects-codegen`, `craftbridge-effects-conformance`, `uniffi-bindgen`, `xtask` | anything; nothing depends on a tool |

Every row may also take external crates that are no Craft app's.

- A core crate never depends on an `effectcraft-*` crate or on an app crate, not even in its tests (PD9). An app crate never depends on another app's crates, not even in its tests: code two plugins need moves into the core (PD18). The rank and `uniffi` rules are about what ships, so dev-dependencies, which only a crate's own tests compile, are outside them; the tool rule is not, since a tool may reach every app, and a test that took one would reach them through it. A Craft app's crate is known by its name or by the app's repository it comes from.
- `uniffi` appears only in `-ffi` crates, and only an app's `-ffi` crate builds a `staticlib` or `cdylib`, and it builds both; no crate is a Rust `dylib` (D-4).
- Every crate is a workspace member in the folder its row gives it (`core/<name>`, `<app>/<name>`, or `<name>` for a tool that is no app's), its library and binaries named after it, and a core crate's name carries none of the Craft apps' nouns, because the core serves them all; a dependency by a path outside the workspace, or on a workspace crate's name from anywhere else, is refused, and so is every local package of the resolved graph, every feature on, that is no member (a path, `[patch]` or `[replace]` brings it in), and every `Cargo.toml` under `rust/` but the workspace's and its members'.
- Swift: `CraftBridgeFFI` ← `CraftBridge` ← `CraftBridgeEffects`. Kotlin: `:effects` exposes `:core`. Swift and Kotlin take the same rule as Rust: a plugin target or plugin module depends only on the core (in Swift, the core's targets `CraftBridge`, the generated `CraftBridgeFFI` and its binary target), `CraftBridge` and `:core` depend on no plugin, and no plugin depends on another; the package manifest, read by `swift package dump-package`, and Gradle's own project graph, declared and resolved, enforce this. A platform folder never refers to another platform's code; every platform reads `conformance/`.
- Code and data a generator in this repository writes live only in `generated` or `Generated` directories, carry an `@generated` header where the format has comments (in Markdown, an HTML comment; JSON, CSV, plain text and binary files need none), are committed, and are written only by `cargo xtask generate` (D-26, L10); a marker anywhere else, the root's own files included, is a generated file in the wrong place. Three kinds of written-for-you file are outside that rule: what a build tool writes for itself (`Cargo.lock`, `Package.resolved`, the Gradle wrapper), which change only through that tool; the `[patch.crates-io]` and `[profile.release]` tables of `rust/Cargo.toml` and the starting `Cargo.lock`, which only `tools/update-upstream.sh` writes from the pinned EffectCraft (Pins, below); and the plan's views in `plan/`, which the plan kit builds from this file and `plan/diagrams/src/`: the gate's Plan stage rebuilds those views from their sources and fails on any byte that differs, bar the drawing in each diagram's SVG export, which only draw.io Desktop writes (the gate, below), and `plan/plan check --final` checks this file against the plan's own writing rules and reports a view older than what builds it.

**Pins.** `[workspace.dependencies]` names each EffectCraft crate CraftBridge uses (`effectcraft-engine`, `-host`, `-automation`, `-gpu`, `-render`, `-time`, `-text`, `-media`, `-expr`, `-script`, `-plugin`) with `git = "https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft"` and one `rev`, an official revision (`10376058` at the start, PD4, PD17), and `filmcraft-codecs` and `filmcraft-isobmff` with EffectCraft's own FilmCraft revision `d5ead4ba` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:89-90`), so CraftBridge's decoders register into the same registry EffectCraft decodes through (D-13).

- Cargo applies `[patch]` tables only at the root workspace, so EffectCraft's own `[patch.crates-io]` entries (`hayro-syntax`, `hayro-jbig2` and the egui family, `effectcraft: Cargo.toml:223-239`) and its `[profile.release]` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:219-221`) are **generated** into `rust/Cargo.toml` from the pinned upstream `Cargo.toml` by `tools/update-upstream.sh`, and `Cargo.lock` starts from the pinned upstream `Cargo.lock`. No line of them is written by hand (D-21).
- Nothing in EffectCraft is changed, and CraftBridge never builds from a fork or a patched branch; the fork `ChristopherLinnett/effectcraft` is only kept in step with upstream (PD17).

**The adaptations** (PD5, D-29). Where a phone needs EffectCraft to do something differently, CraftBridge does it in its own crates on EffectCraft's public interfaces, never by copying EffectCraft code. `tools/adaptations.toml` lists each adaptation with the EffectCraft files and items it relies on, so the update script names the adaptations an update touches (§24).

**States.**
- *Pinned*: `rev` is an official storytold/effectcraft commit; `info` reports it as `pin`.
- *Update in progress*: the update script has moved the pin and named the adaptations whose EffectCraft code changed; the update merges once each named adaptation is rechecked and the gate passes (§24).

**Edge cases.**
- An update changes code an adaptation follows (a new `render` flag, a renamed command an adaptation calls): the script names the adaptation; `RenderRequest` gains the field and the corpus the scenario, in the same update.
- An update removes a public item an adaptation uses: the build fails at the gate, and the adaptation is rewritten on what upstream offers instead, in the same update.
- Upstream adds a public interface that does what an adaptation does (a session with explicit folders, an encoder interface): the adaptation moves onto it and leaves `tools/adaptations.toml` (upstream wins).

**The gate.** `tools/ci.sh` is the one entry point for people, agents and CI (D-25). Before any stage it refuses a Rust toolchain other than the one `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` pins, any rustup override of `rust/`, and an environment that switches what the Rust tools check (a rustflags or rustdocflags variable, a compiler, wrapper, rustdoc or rustfmt, a runner or linker, a profile or alias override, another lockfile, `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP`, `CLIPPY_CONF_DIR`), naming the variable — and the same switches written as keys in any Cargo configuration Cargo reads for a build in `rust/` are refused the same way: one table, `tools/refused-switches.tsv`, names every switch by its configuration key and the variables Cargo derives from it, the environment check and the rules' key check read that one table, and the rules name the file and the key — and reads the pins of both pin files through `cargo xtask pins`, from an xtask it built in that run. It runs `tools/doctor.sh --gate`, then the rules, which need no build, before any stage compiles the workspace (so no build script runs before the gate has judged whether it may exist), then every other stage, and one run reports every failure; `tools/ci.sh <stage or group>…` runs only those named, every name checked before the first runs.

| Stage | Checks |
|---|---|
| Rust | `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -D warnings` of what ships, and of the tests with the two calls-by-path lints taken back; the never-crash calls also named by path in `rust/clippy.toml` (`disallowed-methods`, `disallowed-macros`), which reach a macro's expansion and a method taken as a value; `cargo test --workspace`; `cargo clippy -D warnings` of the libraries for each of the four mobile targets, in the dev and the release profile, so the platform modules, which only the phones compile, and code only the release build holds meet the never-crash lints and carry their `// SAFETY:` comments; every file each of these compilations reads, from the compiler's dep-info (`cargo xtask compiled`), one of its crate's own `.rs` files the rules read, so no `#[path]`, `include!` or `include_str!` reaches another; `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` over every feature; no cargo stage runs while the repository root holds a `.cargo` folder |
| Rules | `cargo xtask rules`: one reading of every file (text UTF-8 with no NUL, paths in NFC, known names and endings spelt the canonical way, no symbolic link, no Rust, Swift, Kotlin or shell outside the code folders but `plan/plan` and the probes kept in `plan/evidence/`); the root and platform-folder layout, with no `node_modules` in the code folders, no hand-written Java under `android/sdk` (whose never-crash and JNI rules are written for Kotlin alone), and no platform build file — a `Cargo.toml`, a `Package.swift`, a Gradle build or settings file — anywhere the repository holds it but its own platform folder and the plan's evidence; layers and dependency direction over the resolved graph with every feature, no local package outside the workspace however it is brought in, in Swift too (the manifest, read by `swift package dump-package`), with no plugin depending on a plugin, every regular target at `Sources/<name>` as `swift package describe` resolves it, moved by no `path:` and found in no other source folder, and every Swift target built and compiling only files the checks read (`swift package describe`); the inherited lint table, its five no-exception lints `forbid`, weakened by no crate, module, item (bar `expect_used`'s literal), clippy configuration, Cargo configuration, target runner or compiler wrapper, with a build script (as `cargo metadata` reports it) only for a crate the layer table marks, every crate inheriting the workspace edition with `edition.workspace = true`, no target table writing an edition of its own, and `cargo metadata`'s resolved edition, the crate's and each of its targets', the workspace's, and `panic = "unwind"`; `unsafe` only in a platform crate's own `src/platform/` (D-20), read from Rust's syntax tree by `syn` once OPS-8 lands (D-28); generated-file placement; one copy of each gate configuration, and none of the tool configurations that would switch a check off (Gate machinery, below); the licences of what the builds use — every external module resolved onto a Gradle library module's release, unit-test and instrumented-test runtime classpaths, or onto the tool classpaths of the detekt the gate runs its Kotlin checks with (the rule project's compile, runtime and test classpaths, and the analyser's own), every package a `Package.swift` names (as `swift package dump-package` reads it) and every pin a `Package.resolved` records, committed whenever the package takes a published one, each declared in `tools/licences.toml`, with build plugins checked by name from the catalog's `[plugins]`; one copy of each EffectCraft, FilmCraft and Craft library crate (D-13), bar a Craft library crate the pinned EffectCraft's own lock already resolves at two official revisions, held to exactly that split; the EffectCraft pin a commit official main reaches, named by its id, the generated tables exactly what `tools/update-upstream.sh` writes, every EffectCraft, FilmCraft and Craft library package of `Cargo.lock` from a source the pin sanctions, down to the commit Cargo builds, and no Cargo configuration Cargo reads for a build in `rust/` — the repository's own, those in every folder above the checkout, the cargo home's, whatever those `include`, and the environment the gate runs in — holds a `[patch]`, `paths` or a `[source]` replacement, nor a refused switch written as a key: the one table `tools/refused-switches.tsv` names every refused switch by its configuration key and the variables Cargo derives from it — rustflags and rustdocflags, a compiler and its wrappers, rustdoc, runners, linkers, a dependency's build-script override and every other target key, profiles, aliases, the build target, another lockfile than the committed one, and every `[env]` entry — and the committed `rust/.cargo/config.toml` may set only what it holds today: the `xtask` alias, and only while it still runs the xtask package; the file and key are named for each, and because both the environment check and the key check read that one table, neither can drift from the other (Pins) |
| Generated | `cargo xtask generate --check`: everything regenerated, any difference fails, and so does a file there git does not track (L10) |
| Plan | `cargo xtask plan-views --check`: the plan kit's own builders, `build/build-diagrams.mjs` then `build/build-plan.mjs` as `plan/package.json` names them, rebuild every view from this file and `plan/diagrams/src/` into a scratch copy of the plan's files (git's, so the ignore files alone say what is no part of the plan), and any byte that differs fails, named — so a view edited by hand fails here whatever its time says, and no list of the views is kept to fall out of date. It runs on Node and `npm ci` in `plan/` and nothing else: `--no-shots` keeps a browser down (this plan builds no mockup gallery), and the diagram build runs with the absolute path of `true` as draw.io's exporter (`DRAWIO_BIN`, which the kit passes over for draw.io Desktop when it names no file the kit can find), so each `.drawio` and the kit's trimming of each SVG export are weighed and no app starts; an export in the diagrams' folder that no source builds any more fails too, since nothing would rebuild it again. The drawing in each SVG export is the one thing it cannot weigh: it is draw.io Desktop's own rendering, holding no copy of the diagram, and no version here pins that app; a hand edit to one still fails through the HTML, which inlines it, until the HTML is rebuilt, and `plan/plan check --final` reports an export older than its source |
| Swift | `swift format lint --strict` on every Swift file the rules' walk lists, whose never-crash rules (force unwraps and `as!`, `try!`, implicitly unwrapped optionals) neither its configuration nor a file-wide `swift-format-ignore-file` switches off, and whose own test exemption reaches only the files SwiftPM compiles into its test targets (`swift package describe`): `import XCTest` is refused everywhere and Swift Testing outside a test target; `cargo xtask swift-lint`: SwiftLint's built-in `missing_docs` on every `open` and `public` declaration, protocol requirements and enum cases included, and the rest read through SourceKit-LSP with SwiftPM's settings for every build of the package that ships — Debug and Release for each Apple slice `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` builds the native library for, the iOS device and the iOS Simulator — so each `#if` branch a shipping build compiles is read resolved and the compiler's own tokens, symbols and declarations say what a name means: neither a Swift 6 regex literal nor a comment hides code and no plain-text scan is left to be fooled (SwiftLint's custom rules lex Swift 5, where `/\/*/` opens a comment): outside test targets the never-crash calls (`fatalError`, `exit`, `abort` and the like, called or taken as a value, however qualified) unless they resolve to a declaration of ours, every postfix `!` and `.unsafelyUnwrapped`; in tests too the pointer APIs, a pointer type reached through a type alias (ours or the SDK's) and a binding to a C symbol confined to `Platform/`; everywhere a `swiftlint:` command, and a swift-format ignore that switches a never-crash rule off file-wide, switches every rule off, reaches beyond one function or property, or gives no reason (D-28); every target, test targets included (`build build-for-testing`), built in Debug and in Release for each Apple slice `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` names, the iOS device and the iOS Simulator, as `cargo xtask swift-builds` lists them from the table the Swift checks read (the rules refuse a regular target no product and no test target uses, which the scheme would not build), with an import the package does not declare an error (`DIAGNOSE_MISSING_TARGET_DEPENDENCIES=YES_ERROR`), so `CraftBridge` cannot import a plugin |
| Android | Spotless (ktlint, from the root `.editorconfig` alone, run every time and never replayed from a cache, in a Gradle build of its own: ktlint sets and puts back IntelliJ's JVM-wide path settings as it starts, which crashes a Lint starting in the same JVM), detekt for the never-crash calls, the JNI declarations confined to `platform/` in every source set, the package every module's own files and its generated bindings declare, and the refusal of a suppression written over a whole file or switching a gate rule off on an item, read from Kotlin's own syntax tree with its types resolved (D-28), Android Lint on the debug and the release variant, the release build and the unit-test and instrumented-test Kotlin compilations, with warnings as errors, and explicit API mode on the library code (Kotlin exempts tests from it, and Lint runs only its test checks there); the build itself refuses a module that skips the convention plugin or sets its rules back, a check the gate asks for that no longer brings the tasks doing its work, and a project dependency, declared or resolved, from `:core` on any module or from a plugin module on anything but `:core`; a task any module disables or skips with `onlyIf` reports SKIPPED, which `cargo xtask skipped-tasks` reads from Gradle's log and fails the stage on |
| Shell | `shellcheck --norc` on every script the rules' walk lists, told by its `.sh` ending or a `#!` line naming sh, bash, dash or ksh, bar the Gradle wrapper, which Gradle writes; `plan/` holds no script but the plan kit's `plan/plan` and the probes kept in `plan/evidence/` |
| Duplicates | jscpd over Rust, Swift, Kotlin and shell: a block of ten lines, or of seventy tokens, repeated anywhere fails, in two passes because jscpd applies its two minimums together; jscpd reads the rules' own file list, which leaves out generated directories and build output and nothing else (`plan/` holds none of the four languages but `plan/plan` and the probes kept in `plan/evidence/`), with every script the shell stage checks named to it as bash; jscpd runs with `--no-gitignore`, and the rules refuse the `.ignore` files, nested `.gitignore` files and ignore markers it would honour |
| Conformance | the desktop corpus (§28), from QA-1 on |

Until OPS-8 lands, `cargo xtask rules` reads `unsafe` and lint attributes in Rust on text with its comments and literals stripped (OPS-3); that task moves its checks onto the language's syntax tree and out of the rules stage.

**Gate machinery.** The gate's own machinery decides what the gate checks, so it cannot guard itself: `tools/ci.sh`, `tools/env.sh`, `tools/refused-switches.tsv`, `tools/hooks/`, `rust/xtask/`, `rust/.cargo/config.toml`, `android/sdk/settings.gradle.kts`, `android/sdk/gradle.properties`, `android/sdk/build-logic/`, and the single copy of each of `rust/clippy.toml`, `rust/rustfmt.toml`, `rust/deny.toml`, `ios/sdk/.swift-format`, `ios/sdk/.swiftlint.yml`, `tools/licences.toml` and the root `.editorconfig`. A change to any of those files is a gate change, which its pull request names and whose review checks for weakened rules; the gate fails on a second copy of any listed configuration file, or of a tool configuration that would act like one, anywhere in the tree (AGENTS §10, decision #120): clippy reads `clippy.toml` or `.clippy.toml` and rustfmt `rustfmt.toml` or `.rustfmt.toml` nearest a crate, cargo-deny's `deny.exceptions.toml` and `.deny.exceptions.toml` widen `rust/deny.toml`'s allowlist, ktlint merges every `.editorconfig` up to the root's, and Cargo reads a `rust/.cargo/config` in place of `config.toml`. Tool configurations the gate keeps none of fail it wherever they sit: `.shellcheckrc` and `shellcheckrc`, which shellcheck reads as directives (it also runs with `--norc`), `.ignore` and any `.gitignore` but the root's and `plan/.gitignore`, which jscpd honours (it also runs with `--no-gitignore`), a jscpd ignore marker in the code folders, and a `.sourcekit-lsp` folder, whose configuration SourceKit-LSP merges over the options the Swift stage starts it with. Gradle reads a `gradle.properties` in a project's own folder as that project's properties, so no other `gradle.properties` sits under `android/sdk`: the build's own is `android/sdk/gradle.properties` alone, and `android/sdk/build-logic`, an included build with properties of its own, is where its own may sit (AGENTS §10, decision #122).

**Module build files.** An Android module's build file applies the convention plugin and names its namespace once, and holds only comments, `plugins { id("craftbridge.android.library") }`, `android { namespace = "io.github.christopherlinnett.craftbridge.<module>" }` and a `dependencies` block whose entries are `api`, `implementation`, `testImplementation` or `androidTestImplementation` of a `project(":…")` or a `libs.<alias>`; the root `android/sdk/build.gradle.kts` holds only comments and a `plugins` block of `alias(libs.plugins.<alias>) apply false` lines and `id("craftbridge.quality")`. Every module the settings include has its build file, spelled exactly `build.gradle.kts` because a case-insensitive disk would hand Gradle a `Build.gradle.kts` all the same, no build file is written in Groovy — Gradle would read `build.gradle` in place of `build.gradle.kts`, and the rule reads only Kotlin — and anything else a build needs is configured once in `android/sdk/build-logic`, so a module's file never carries the reach to rewire a check the gate relies on (AGENTS §10, decision #121).
